sayAlt.hi: Apni dono baahein V ki tarah phailao, aur phir haathon mein do lambi lakdiyan pakad lo. Baahein ab lambi lagti hain, par kandhe par unke beech ka khulna wahi hai, toh angle bhi wahi hai.
sayAlt.en: Spread both your arms like a V, and then hold two long sticks in your hands. Your arms now look longer, but the opening between them at your shoulders is the same, so the angle is the same too.

simpler.hi: Bhujayein lambi karne se angle zyada nahi khulta. Angle sirf khulne se bada hota hai.
simpler.en: Making the arms longer does not open the angle wider. An angle grows only by opening.

prompt.hi: Do khuli kainchiyon ke blade 4 cm aur 16 cm ke hain. Kiska angle bada hai?
prompt.en: Two open pairs of scissors have blades of 4 cm and 16 cm. Whose angle is bigger?

reask.hi: Board par 4 cm wali aur 16 cm wali kainchi khuli hai; in dono mein angle kiska bada hai?
reask.en: On the board, scissors with 4 cm and with 16 cm blades are open; which of the two has the bigger angle?

viewCaption.hi: Ab dono kainchiyon ke kone par tester ka kona rakha hai, aur uska ek seedha kinaara ek blade ke saath. Ab har kainchi ka doosra blade dekho.
viewCaption.en: Now the tester's corner is laid on the corner of both pairs of scissors, with one straight edge along one blade. Now look at each pair's other blade.

why.hi: 4 cm blade wali kainchi zyada khuli hai aur 16 cm blade wali kam, toh 4 cm wali ka angle bada hai
why.en: the scissors with 4 cm blades open more and the 16 cm ones less, so the 4 cm scissors' angle is bigger

whyShort.hi: 4 cm wali zyada khuli, toh uska angle bada
whyShort.en: the 4 cm pair opens more: a bigger angle

whyAlt.hi: 16 cm ke lambe blade sirf blade lambe karte hain; khulna dekho, lambai nahi
whyAlt.en: the long 16 cm blades only make the blades longer; look at the opening, not the length

simpler.hi: Blade ki lambai mat dekho. Sirf yeh dekho ki tester ke mukable kaun kitni khuli hai.
simpler.en: Do not look at the blade length. Just see how far each pair opens compared with the tester.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab ek aisi shape aayegi jismein koi kona hi nahi hota: circle, jise hum string se banayenge.
bridgeToNext.en: Next comes a shape with no corner at all: the circle, which we will draw with a string.

simpler.hi: Ab bina kone wali shape, circle, banayenge.
simpler.en: Next we draw a shape with no corner, the circle.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein circle aaya: uske kinaare ka har point centre se barabar door hota hai.
covered.en: Last came the circle: every point on its edge is equally far from the centre.

hook.convey: draw round a bangle, or mark a big circle in the playground with a rope and chalk → a circle has a centre, and every point on it is the same distance from the centre

use.hi: Drawing ke liye chudi kaagaz par rakho aur uske kinaare par pencil ghumao: jo shape banegi, woh circle hai.
use.en: For a drawing, put a bangle on paper and run a pencil round its edge: the shape you get is a circle.

use.hi: Playground mein game ke liye bada circle banana hai. Rassi aur chalk se woh kaise banega, aaj dekhenge.
use.en: A big circle is needed in the playground for a game. Today we see how a rope and chalk make it.

explain.convey: string compass: one end of the string held still = the centre, a pencil at the other end, string kept tight → the pencil stays one string-length from the centre everywhere; asked: one edge point is 4 cm away, how far is another

viewCaption.hi: Ab centre se kinaare tak string teen alag jagah kheenchi hai.
viewCaption.en: Now the string is drawn from the centre to the edge at three different places.

point.hi: String ka ek sira dabao: yahi centre hai. Doosre sire ki pencil ko string tight rakh kar ghumao; pencil har jagah centre se string jitni door rehti hai.
point.en: Hold one end of the string down: that is the centre. Turn the pencil at the other end with the string kept tight; everywhere, the pencil stays one string-length from the centre.

pointAlt.hi: Khoonte se bandhi ek bakri socho, jo rassi tight karke chaaron taraf ghoomti hai. Woh har baar khoonte se rassi jitni door hi pahunchti hai, aur uske chalne se ek circle ban jaata hai.
pointAlt.en: Picture a goat tied to a peg, walking all the way round with the rope tight. Each time it gets exactly one rope-length from the peg, and its path makes a circle.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke kinaare ka ek point centre se 4 cm door hai. {friend} ke hisaab se doosra point 5 cm door hai. Kya aisa ho sakta hai?
prompt.en: One point on this circle's edge is 4 cm from the centre. By {friend}'s reckoning another point is 5 cm away. Can that happen?

reask.hi: Jis circle ke kinaare ka ek point centre se 4 cm door hai, kya uska koi doosra point 5 cm door ho sakta hai?
reask.en: On a circle with an edge point 4 cm from the centre, can another edge point be 5 cm away?

accept: no, it is also 4 cm away

why.hi: kinaare ka har point centre se string jitna door hai, toh har point 4 cm door hai, 5 cm nahi
why.en: every edge point is one string-length from the centre, so every point is 4 cm away, not 5 cm

whyShort.hi: kinaare ka har point 4 cm door, 5 cm nahi
whyShort.en: every edge point is 4 cm away, not 5 cm

whyAlt.hi: ghumate waqt string ki lambai nahi badalti; 4 cm ki string pencil ko 5 cm tak le hi nahi ja sakti
whyAlt.en: the string's length does not change as it goes round; a 4 cm string can never take the pencil out to 5 cm

simpler.hi: Socho, string tight rakhne par pencil kabhi centre ke paas aati hai ya door jaati hai kya.
simpler.en: Think whether, with the string tight, the pencil ever comes closer to the centre or goes further.

simpler.hi: String tight rahe, toh pencil centre se hamesha string jitni hi door rehti hai.
simpler.en: While the string stays tight, the pencil always stays as far from the centre as the string is long.

explain.convey: a coin: every edge point equally far from its centre → a circle; a round thing whose distance changes → round, but not a circle; asked: a roti 8 cm one way, 10 cm the other, its two distances on the board

viewCaption.hi: Board par sikka bana hai: beech mein centre, aur centre se kinaare tak ek teer, jis par barabar door likha hai.
viewCaption.en: The board shows the coin: the centre in the middle, and an arrow from the centre to the edge marked equally far.

point.hi: Sikke ka har kinaare wala point centre se barabar door hai, isliye sikka circle hai. Jis gol cheez mein yeh doori badle, woh circle nahi.
point.en: Every point on a coin's edge is equally far from its centre, so a coin is a circle. A round thing where this distance changes is not a circle.

pointAlt.hi: Ek nimbu dekho: woh gol dikhta hai, par uske centre se kinaara ek taraf door hai aur doosri taraf paas. Isliye nimbu gol hai, circle nahi; sikke mein yeh doori har taraf ek jaisi hai.
pointAlt.en: Look at a lemon: it looks round, but its edge is far from the centre one way and near the other. So a lemon is round, not a circle; in a coin this distance is the same every way.

prompt.hi: Ek roti ke centre se kinaara ek taraf 8 cm door hai aur doosri taraf 10 cm. Kya yeh roti circle hai?
prompt.en: From the centre of a roti, the edge is 8 cm away one way and 10 cm the other. Is this roti a circle?

reask.hi: Jis roti ka kinaara centre se ek taraf 8 cm aur doosri taraf 10 cm door hai, kya woh circle hai?
reask.en: Is a roti whose edge is 8 cm from the centre one way and 10 cm the other a circle?

accept: no, the distances are not equal

why.hi: sikka circle hai, kyunki kinaara har taraf barabar door hai; roti ka 8 cm aur 10 cm, toh circle nahi
why.en: a coin is a circle, its edge equally far every way; the roti's is 8 cm and 10 cm, so no

whyShort.hi: doori 8 cm aur 10 cm, barabar nahi
whyShort.en: the distances are 8 cm and 10 cm, not equal

whyAlt.hi: circle hoti toh roti ka kinaara har taraf centre se utna hi door hota, jitna sikke mein; yahan ek taraf kinaara zyada door hai
whyAlt.en: if it were a circle the roti's edge would be just as far every way, as in a coin; here the edge is further one way

simpler.hi: Dono taraf ki doori aapas mein milao, aur yaad karo ki circle mein yeh doori kaisi hoti hai.
simpler.en: Compare the two distances with each other, and remember what this distance is like in a circle.

pictureCaption.hi: Yeh roti ki dono dooriyan hain, centre se kinaare tak: ek taraf 8 cm, doosri taraf 10 cm.
pictureCaption.en: These are the roti's two distances, from the centre to the edge: 8 cm one way, 10 cm the other.

simpler.hi: Circle ki pehchaan doori se hoti hai: centre se kinaare tak har taraf ek jaisi doori.
simpler.en: A circle is known by its distance: the same distance from the centre to the edge every way.

explain.convey: playground circle: a 3 m rope tied to a peg, chalk at the other end, rope kept tight → every chalk mark is 3 m from the peg; asked: of marks 3 m, 4 m and 3 m away, which is not on this circle

viewCaption.hi: Ab khoonte se kinaare tak 3 m ki rassi teen alag jagah dikhayi hai.
viewCaption.en: Now the 3 m rope is shown from the peg to the edge at three different places.

point.hi: Khoonte se 3 m ki rassi baandho, aur doosre sire par chalk. Rassi tight rakhkar chalo, toh chalk ka har nishaan khoonte se 3 m door aata hai.
point.en: Tie a 3 m rope to a peg, with chalk at the other end. Walk round keeping the rope tight, and every chalk mark comes 3 m from the peg.

pointAlt.hi: Rassi beech mein dheeli ho jaaye, toh chalk khoonte ke paas aa jaata hai aur shape bigad jaati hai. Tight rassi har nishaan ko khoonte se barabar door rakhti hai, aur wahi sahi circle banata hai.
pointAlt.en: If the rope goes slack, the chalk comes closer to the peg and the shape goes wrong. A tight rope keeps every mark equally far from the peg, and that makes a true circle.

prompt.hi: Zameen par teen nishaan hain: khoonte se 1 m, 3 m aur 5 m door. Inmein se kitne nishaan is circle par nahi hain?
prompt.en: There are three marks on the ground: 1 m, 3 m and 5 m from the peg. How many of these marks are not on this circle?

reask.hi: Khoonte se 1 m, 3 m aur 5 m door ke nishaanon mein se kitne nishaan 3 m rassi wale circle par nahi hain?
reask.en: Of the marks 1 m, 3 m and 5 m from the peg, how many are not on the circle made with the 3 m rope?

why.hi: 3 m rassi se har nishaan 3 m door banta hai; 1 m aur 5 m wale 2 nishaan circle par nahi
why.en: a 3 m rope keeps every mark 3 m away; the 2 marks at 1 m and 5 m are off it

whyShort.hi: circle par har nishaan 3 m door hai
whyShort.en: every mark on the circle is 3 m away

whyAlt.hi: tight 3 m rassi chalk ko na 1 m par rukne deti hai, na 5 m tak le jaati hai
whyAlt.en: a tight 3 m rope neither lets the chalk stop at 1 m nor carries it out to 5 m

simpler.hi: Rassi ki lambai yaad karo, aur har nishaan ki doori usse milao.
simpler.en: Remember the rope's length, and compare each mark's distance with it.

simpler.hi: Rassi 3 m ki hai aur tight hai, toh chalk har baar khoonte se 3 m par hi nishaan banata hai.
simpler.en: The rope is 3 m and tight, so the chalk always makes its mark 3 m from the peg.

problem.hi: Pooja 50 cm ki tight string se rangoli ka circle banati hai. Phir ek kinaare se centre se hote hue doosre kinaare tak seedhi line kheenchti hai.
problem.en: Pooja draws a rangoli circle with a tight 50 cm string. Then she draws a straight line from one edge, through the centre, to the other edge.

problemAlt.hi: Pooja ki string ka ek sira centre par tha aur doosre par chalk. Hum us seedhi line ki lambai nikalenge jo ek kinaare se chalkar centre se guzarti hai aur doosre kinaare par rukti hai.
problemAlt.en: One end of Pooja's string was at the centre and the chalk at the other. We will find the length of the straight line that starts at one edge, passes through the centre and stops at the other edge.

simpler.hi: Pehle ek chhoti baat yaad karo: tight rassi ka har nishaan khoonte se rassi jitna door aata tha. Pooja ki string bhi waise hi kaam karti hai.
simpler.en: First recall a small one: every mark of a tight rope came one rope-length from the peg. Pooja's string works just the same way.

givens.hi: String ki lambai, aur centre se hokar jaane wali line.
givens.en: The string's length, and the line through the centre.

find.hi: centre se hokar jaane wali line ki lambai
find.en: the length of the line through the centre

prompt.hi: Rangoli ke kinaare ka koi bhi point centre se kitni door hai?
prompt.en: How far from the centre is any point on the rangoli's edge?

right.hi: Bilkul, 50 cm: tight string har point ko utna hi door rakhti hai.
right.en: Exactly, 50 cm: the tight string keeps every point just that far.

reask.hi: Pooja ki tight string se bane kinaare par chalk ka har nishaan centre se kitna door padta hai?
reask.en: On the edge drawn with Pooja's tight string, how far from the centre does each chalk mark fall?

do.hi: Kinaare ki centre se doori dekho
do.en: Look at the edge's distance from the centre

why.hi: tight string kinaare ke har point ko centre se string jitna door rakhti hai
why.en: the tight string keeps every edge point one string-length from the centre

simpler.hi: Yaad karo, chalk kinaare tak kaise pahuncha: string ke ek sire par, jabki doosra sira centre par tha.
simpler.en: Remember how the chalk reached the edge: on one end of the string, while the other end was at the centre.

told.hi: Tight string chalk ko centre se hamesha string jitna, yaani 50 cm, door rakhti hai; toh kinaare ka har point centre se 50 cm door hai.
told.en: The tight string always keeps the chalk a string's length, 50 cm, from the centre; so every point on the edge is 50 cm from the centre.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: ek kinaare se doosre kinaare tak poori line kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: Your turn: how long is the whole line from one edge to the other?

reask.hi: 50 cm string wale circle mein kinaare se centre se hote hue kinaare tak line kitni lambi hai?
reask.en: In a circle drawn with a 50 cm string, how long is the line from edge through the centre to edge?

why.hi: line mein centre ke dono taraf 50 cm hai, toh 50 + 50 = 100 cm
why.en: the line has 50 cm on each side of the centre, so 50 + 50 = 100 cm

whyAlt.hi: line centre se do string jitni doori jodti hai, aur string 50 cm ki hai, toh poori line 100 cm, yaani 1 metre
whyAlt.en: the line joins two string-lengths through the centre, and the string is 50 cm, so the whole line is 100 cm, that is 1 metre

simpler.hi: Line centre par rukti nahi; woh centre ke us paar bhi kinaare tak jaati hai.
simpler.en: The line does not stop at the centre; it goes on past the centre to the edge on the other side.

answer.en: the whole line is 100 cm long

why.hi: centre se hokar jaane wali line mein string jitni doori do baar aati hai
why.en: a line through the centre holds the string's length twice

viewCaption.hi: Ab rangoli ke centre se kinaare tak string teen alag jagah kheenchi hai.
viewCaption.en: Now the string is drawn from the rangoli's centre to its rim at three different places.

prompt.hi: Rangoli ke liye {friend} ne haath se ek gol banaya, aur Pooja ne khoonte aur tight string se. Inmein se pakka circle kiska hai?
prompt.en: For a rangoli, {friend} drew a round shape by hand, and Pooja drew one with a peg and a tight string. Whose is surely a circle?

reask.hi: Haath se bane gol aur tight string se bane gol mein, pakka circle kaunsa hai?
reask.en: Of a round shape drawn by hand and one drawn with a tight string, which is surely a circle?

did.hi: haath ke gol aur string ke circle mein fark pehchana
did.en: told a hand-drawn round shape from a string circle

viewCaption.hi: Ab rangoli ke centre se kinaare tak teen alag jagah teer bane hain, har ek par barabar likha hai.
viewCaption.en: Now arrows are drawn from the rangoli's centre to its rim at three different places, each marked equal.

why.hi: Pooja ne tight string se banaya, toh har point barabar door hai; haath se bane gol mein doori badal sakti hai
why.en: Pooja used a tight string, so every point is equally far; in a round shape drawn by hand the distance can change

whyShort.hi: tight string har point ko barabar door rakhti hai
whyShort.en: a tight string keeps every point equally far

whyAlt.hi: haath se banate waqt pencil kahin centre ke paas aa sakti hai, kahin door ja sakti hai; string tight ho toh aisa nahi hota
whyAlt.en: drawing by hand, the pencil can come nearer the centre in one place and go further in another; with a tight string that cannot happen

simpler.hi: Gol dikhna kaafi nahi hai. Socho, kiski shape mein har point centre se pakka ek jitna door rahega.
simpler.en: Looking round is not enough. Think in whose shape every point will surely stay the same distance from the centre.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne ek gol ghadi ke centre se uske kinaare tak kai jagah naapa, aur har baar 7 cm aaya. Kya ghadi ka kinaara circle hai?
prompt.en: {friend} measured from a round clock's centre to its edge at many places, and got 7 cm every time. Is the clock's edge a circle?

reask.hi: Jis ghadi ke centre se kinaare tak har jagah 7 cm aaya, kya uska kinaara circle hai?
reask.en: If a clock measures 7 cm from its centre to its edge everywhere, is its edge a circle?

did.hi: naap se ghadi ke kinaare ko circle pehchana
did.en: used measuring to tell that a clock's edge is a circle

viewCaption.hi: Ab ghadi ke centre se kinaare tak teen alag jagah naap dikhaya hai.
viewCaption.en: Now the measure from the clock's centre to its edge is shown at three different places.

why.hi: ghadi par jitni jagah naapa, har jagah 7 cm aaya; circle mein kinaare ka har point centre se barabar door hota hai
why.en: wherever the clock was measured it was 7 cm; on a circle every rim point is equally far from the centre

whyShort.hi: har jagah 7 cm, yaani barabar door
whyShort.en: 7 cm everywhere, so equally far

whyAlt.hi: agar kahin naap 7 cm se kam ya zyada aata, tab woh circle na hota; yahan har baar 7 cm aaya
whyAlt.en: if anywhere the measure came less or more than 7 cm, it would not be a circle; here it was 7 cm every time

simpler.hi: Har jagah naap ek hi aaya. Yaad karo, circle ke kinaare ki centre se doori kaisi hoti hai.
simpler.en: Every measurement came out the same. Remember what a circle's edge is like in its distance from the centre.

answerViewCaption.hi: Teeno jagah ghadi ka kinaara centre se 7 cm door hai, isliye ghadi ka kinaara barabar door wala hai, jaisa chahiye.
answerViewCaption.en: At all three places the clock's edge is 7 cm from the centre, so its edge is equally far all round, as it should be.

prompt.hi: Chudi aur anda, dono gol dikhte hain. Inmein se circle kaunsa hai: chudi ya anda?
prompt.en: A bangle and an egg both look round. Which of them is a circle: the bangle or the egg?

did.hi: chudi aur ande mein se circle chuna
did.en: picked the circle out of a bangle and an egg

viewCaption.hi: Ab centre se kinaare tak teen alag jagah teer bane hain, har ek par barabar likha hai.
viewCaption.en: Now arrows are drawn from the centre to the rim at three different places, each marked equal.

why.hi: dono gol hain, par chudi ka kinaara har taraf centre se barabar door hai aur anda ek taraf lamba hai
why.en: both are round, but the bangle's edge is equally far from the centre every way, and the egg is longer one way

whyShort.hi: chudi har taraf barabar, anda ek taraf lamba
whyShort.en: the bangle is even; the egg is long one way

whyAlt.hi: ande ke centre se uski nok tak ki doori, uske pet tak ki doori se zyada hai; chudi mein yeh doori har jagah ek jaisi hai
whyAlt.en: from an egg's centre, its tip is further than its side; in a bangle this distance is the same everywhere

simpler.hi: Dono ke centre se kinaare tak alag-alag taraf socho, aur dekho ki kiski doori har taraf ek jaisi rehti hai.
simpler.en: From the centre of each, think towards the edge in different directions, and see whose distance stays the same every way.

5 cm tight string → every point 5 cm from the pin
why the 2 m rope must stay tight → the same distance from the peg
harder: 6 cm string, marks at 6, 7 and 6 cm → the 7 cm mark is off the circle

remediation.move: string compass (pin, string, pencil) beside a hand-drawn oval → measure from the centre to several points on both → only one has all distances the same; then a string that went slack while drawing

say.hi: Ek circle string se banao, ek oval haath se. Dono mein centre se kinaare tak kai jagah naapo: circle mein har jagah wahi doori aati hai, oval mein doori badalti hai.
say.en: Draw one circle with a string, and an oval by hand. In both, measure the distance from the centre to the edge in many places: in the circle it comes out the same everywhere, in the oval it changes.

viewCaption.hi: Baayein taraf string se bani shape hai jismein har jagah wahi doori hai. Daayein taraf haath ka oval hai, jismein doori badalti hai.
viewCaption.en: On the left is the shape made with a string, with the same distance everywhere. On the right is the hand-drawn oval, where the distance changes.

sayAlt.hi: Ek phoola hua balloon do haathon se dabao, toh woh ek taraf lamba ho jaata hai. Ab uske centre se kinaara ek taraf door hai aur doosri taraf paas, isliye dabaa hua balloon gol hai, par circle nahi.
sayAlt.en: Press a blown-up balloon between your two hands, and it gets longer one way. Now its edge is far from the centre one way and near the other, so the pressed balloon is round, but not a circle.

simpler.hi: Circle mein centre se kinaare tak har jagah ek hi doori hoti hai. Jahan doori badle, woh circle nahi.
simpler.en: In a circle the distance from the centre to the edge is the same everywhere. Where the distance changes, it is not a circle.

prompt.hi: 12 cm ki string ghumate waqt beech mein dheeli ho gayi. Kya bani hui gol shape circle hai?
prompt.en: A 12 cm string went slack partway while going round. Is the round shape that was drawn a circle?

reask.hi: 12 cm string beech mein dheeli ho jaane se bani gol shape kya circle hai?
reask.en: Is the round shape drawn when a 12 cm string went slack partway a circle?

accept: no, it is not a circle

viewCaption.hi: Yeh 12 cm ki tight string se bani shape hai: centre se kinaare tak teen jagah 12 cm. Dheeli string wali shape ko isse milakar socho.
viewCaption.en: This is the shape a tight 12 cm string makes: 12 cm from the centre to the rim at three places. Think of the slack string's shape against this one.

why.hi: string tight nahi rahi, beech mein dheeli hui, toh har point 12 cm door nahi raha: gol hai, circle nahi
why.en: the string did not stay tight, so not every point stayed 12 cm away: round, but not a circle

whyShort.hi: dheeli string se doori 12 cm nahi rahi
whyShort.en: a slack string did not keep 12 cm

whyAlt.hi: dheeli string se pencil centre ke 12 cm se zyada paas aa jaati hai; circle mein woh har jagah 12 cm door rehti
whyAlt.en: with a slack string the pencil comes closer to the centre than 12 cm; on a circle it stays 12 cm away everywhere

simpler.hi: Circle mein har point centre se string jitna door hota hai. Socho, dheeli string se yeh doori har jagah wahi rahegi kya.
simpler.en: In a circle every point is one string-length from the centre. Think whether a slack string keeps that distance the same everywhere.

prompt.hi: Ek square tile ki har bhuja 30 cm hai, aur use ghuma kar tircha rakha hai. Uske ek kone par tester ko tile ke saath ghuma kar rakhoge, toh kona kam khula niklega, bilkul fit hoga, ya zyada khula niklega?
prompt.en: A square tile has sides of 30 cm each, and it has been turned and laid slanting. If you put the tester on one of its corners, turned along with the tile, will the corner come out less open, fit exactly, or come out more open?

did.hi: ghumayi hui, lambi bhuja wali square tile ka kona tester se jaancha
did.en: tested the corner of a turned square tile with long sides

why.hi: tile square hai, toh uska har kona right angle hai; ghumane se kona nahi badalta, aur 30 cm lambi bhuja se kona zyada nahi khulta, isliye tester bilkul fit hoga
why.en: the tile is a square, so each corner is a right angle; turning does not change a corner, and 30 cm long sides do not open it wider, so the tester fits exactly

simpler.hi: Do baatein ek-ek karke socho: tile ko ghumane se uska kona badla kya, aur lambi bhuja se kona zyada khula kya.
simpler.en: Think about two things one at a time: did turning the tile change its corner, and did the long sides open the corner wider.

reask.hi: Ghuma kar rakhi 30 cm wali square tile ke kone par tester bhi ghuma kar rakho: kona kam khula hoga, bilkul fit, ya zyada khula?
reask.en: On the corner of a 30 cm square tile laid turned, put the tester turned too: will the corner be less open, an exact fit, or more open?

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki right angle kitaab ke kone jaisa hota hai, aur ghumane se kona nahi badalta. Phir angle ko uske khulne se naapa, aur circle aaya, jiska har point centre se barabar door hai.
covered.en: Today we saw that a right angle is like a book's corner, and that turning does not change a corner. Then we judged angles by their opening, and met the circle, all of it equally far from its centre.

goodbye.hi: Aaj ke liye itna hi, phir milte hain!
goodbye.en: That's all for today, see you next time!

ask.hi: Aaj ki padhai mein kuch aisa tha jo achha laga?
ask.en: Was there something in today's lesson you liked?

ask.hi: Aaj ka kaam aasaan laga ya thoda mushkil?
ask.en: Did today's work feel easy or a little hard?

ack.hi: Hmm, samajh gayi, batane ke liye shukriya.
ack.en: Hmm, I see; thank you for telling me.

didFrames.hi: Aaj ek kaam tumne khud karke dikhaya: {did}.
didFrames.en: Today you showed one thing yourself: you {did}.
